domains.title: Algorithms from invariants through assembly to C abstractions

objectives.text: Derive an input/output relation, representation invariant and decreasing termination measure for an original bounded state trace.
Compute exact operation counts for contrasting input families and distinguish worst-case, expected and amortized claims with their assumptions.
Find a counterexample to an intentionally weakened invariant and identify the first transition that invalidates it.
Derive byte offsets, valid index ranges and ownership links for reused array/list/stack/queue representations without rebuilding their complete implementations.
Trace the same bounded operation sequence in contiguous and linked representations and account for live storage, traversal work and failed operations.
Explain which representation invariant survives a storage-policy change and verify that no stale reference escapes the selected policy.

subtopics.title: Callable hand-written x86-64 and Thumb kernels

objectives.text: Write original scalar search kernels in separate x86-64 SysV and Cortex-M4 Thumb assembly files and expose checked C declarations.
Derive register liveness, signed/unsigned flag predicates, preserved-register obligations and stack alignment for each kernel and a nested-call probe.
Demonstrate ABI preservation and bounded memory access using adversarial inputs, poisoned scratch registers, sentinels and captured disassembly.
Derive a half-open lower-bound search invariant and progress argument for duplicate, absent and boundary keys.
Translate that invariant into a hand-written assembly kernel with an explicit element width and overflow-safe address calculation.
Compare operation counts with the reused C implementation and reject an off-by-one or signedness mutation with a concrete smallest counterexample.
Derive preservation of the sorted prefix, multiset and tagged equal-key order during bounded insertion and merge transitions.
Write a small original assembly insertion kernel while reusing the prior full merge/heap sort implementations for differential evidence.
Measure comparisons and moves on sorted, reverse and duplicate-rich inputs and separate asymptotic evidence from machine timing.
Derive the local precondition and moving violation for sift-down in the reused zero-origin heap representation.
Replace only the bounded sift-down kernel with original assembly and preserve the prior heap API and duplicate policy.
Recompute heap order and key multiplicity independently after each transition and account for height-bounded work without claiming the whole heap was rebuilt.
Derive inorder, height and balance effects of single and double rotations and of a deletion rebalance path in the prior AVL implementation.
Instrument the reused tree to emit state certificates and verify parent/child reachability, duplicate policy and cached metadata after each mutation.
Compare balanced and degenerate search paths on the same keys and explain the difference between functional equivalence and resource bounds.

subtopics.title: Hash probes and bounded string matching

objectives.text: Derive probe reachability through empty, occupied and deleted slots and identify the assumptions behind expected lookup bounds.
Write a bounded assembly probe/search kernel over the prior hash representation and a small original C byte-span matcher with an explicit empty-pattern policy.
Verify collision, wraparound, full-table, tombstone and embedded-zero cases while counting probes or byte comparisons independently.

subtopics.title: Graph frontiers, shortest paths and historical refinement

objectives.text: Derive the distinction between BFS layers, tentative weighted distances and settled vertices from a small original graph trace.
Reuse the earlier queue and priority heap to implement a bounded graph adapter with nonnegative weights, checked distance addition and disconnected results.
Validate distances and predecessor paths against independent tiny-graph enumeration and explain why a negative edge or an invalid settle rule breaks the chosen argument.

subtopics.title: Higher C abstractions over invariant-preserving kernels

objectives.text: Design a typed wrapper and an explicit context/callback interface over a reused container or new assembly kernel without delegating the educational algorithm to libc.
State ownership, comparator consistency, failure atomicity and iterator invalidation contracts and distinguish pointer collections from byte-copy value storage.
Show identical observable results across the chosen typed and generic adapters, with independently checked lifetime, error and representation evidence.

domains.title: Computer and microcontroller architecture from state to evidence

objectives.text: Define registers, memory, instruction state and external inputs for a small abstract machine and trace its state transitions.
Separate ISA-visible behavior from datapath, pipeline, cache and board integration choices using a paired x86-64/Cortex-M4 comparison.
Classify each claimed observation as a model result, executable ISA result or physical device measurement and record its unresolved assumptions.

subtopics.title: Boolean logic, ALU slices and finite arithmetic

objectives.text: Derive full-adder and subtraction truth tables from Boolean equations and compose a four-bit ripple-carry model.
Compute result, zero, sign, carry and overflow flags for every four-bit input pair and distinguish carry from signed overflow.
Relate the model to inspected x86 and Arm condition flags while explaining why machine wraparound does not establish defined C signed overflow.
Derive effects of byte, word and doubleword operations on complete x86-64 register state and contrast the selected Thumb widths.
Reconstruct values from an explicit little-endian byte sequence and calculate base/index/scale/displacement addresses with bounds.
Demonstrate that aligned addresses, hardware accessibility and C object/effective-type permission are separate obligations in a reused typed or byte-storage example.

subtopics.title: Instruction formats, decoding and branch targets

objectives.text: Decode a bounded selected x86 instruction’s prefix/opcode/operand fields and a selected Thumb instruction’s halfwords from their actual bytes.
Compute relative branch targets and explain the distinction between instruction width, architectural PC behavior and assembler syntax.
Cross-check hand decoding with vendor definitions and disassembly while rejecting a deliberately wrong displacement or width assumption.
Build a small original register/ALU/load/store datapath state model with explicit next-state and commit rules.
Trace fetch, decode, operand selection, execution and update for a declared toy instruction sequence and identify the control signals required.
Explain why the toy model is not a faithful Cortex-M4 or x86 microarchitecture and distinguish combinational output from clocked stored state.

subtopics.title: Pipeline hazards, forwarding and control changes

objectives.text: Produce a stage-by-cycle schedule for a declared five-stage in-order model including a RAW dependency and load-use delay.
Derive the effect of forwarding, a stall and a taken-branch flush on the same instruction stream and count retired instructions and cycles.
Explain why RAW dependence, pipeline hazard and data race are distinct and limit any extrapolation to a physical CPU.

subtopics.title: Memory hierarchy, locality and cache costs

objectives.text: Derive cache index/tag/offset and hit/miss outcomes for a small specified cache and original address trace.
Compute AMAT and a declared in-order stall estimate with consistent units, then compare two layouts without equating misses with execution time.
Identify compulsory, capacity or conflict mechanisms within the stated model and separate model results from measured cache behavior.

subtopics.title: Microcontroller memory, buses and DMA reachability

objectives.text: Map CPU and DMA masters to documented STM32F4 memory targets and explain the CCM versus ordinary SRAM reachability boundary.
Derive a linker-placement and DMA-buffer decision from exact part/revision evidence and document ownership and completion ordering separately.
Trace arbitration and peripheral-bridge constraints in a static model and record which throughput or electrical claims require real device measurements.
Trace reset vector selection and a basic Cortex-M4 exception entry/return state using previously inspected startup and core passages.
Compare a subroutine call’s ABI preservation with exception stacking and priority behavior without treating them as interchangeable.
Verify a saved original frame/return trace and state the limits of emulator observations, optional FP state and device-specific boot configuration.
Compute CPU time and whole-task speedup from original instruction/CPI/frequency and Amdahl inputs with dimensionally checked arithmetic.
Design a bounded experiment comparing reused C and hand-written kernels with identical results, captured toolchain/CPU settings and repeated measurements.
Report the measurement distribution and confounders, distinguish algorithmic work from elapsed time, and avoid emulator-based WCET or energy conclusions.
